instruction:
We act for Trouseind Provisioning Group, Inc., which is buying the stock of a business from Reitaisk Aviation Services, Inc. Trouseind is also the recipient of services under the related transition services agreement. Before we go back to the other side, the client wants to know where it stands across the whole deal package.

Please review everything in the matter folder:
- stock_purchase_agreement_trouseind_reitaisk.md
- escrow_agreement_lanterwick.md
- transition_services_agreement.md
- seller_side_letter_tax_survival.md
- insurance_certificate_cover_letter_cobbelly.md

Then send me a memo that lists each issue you find. For each one, give:
- where it appears (document and section),
- why it matters for Trouseind, and
- the fix you recommend.

Put the items that matter most to the client first. If something needs a business decision from the client rather than a drafting change, say so. If you have questions about the deal background before you finish, let me know.

rubric.text: The response identifies that, read together, the TSA indemnity from Recipient (Trouseind) to Provider (Reitaisk) covers Losses including Provider's own negligence and is excluded from the liability cap, leaving Trouseind with unlimited liability for Reitaisk's own negligence. It locates this in TSA Sections 8.1 and 9.2, explains why this matters to the client, and recommends a fix.

The response identifies that the Escrow Agreement defines Fundamental Representation Claims more narrowly (Sections 3.1, 3.2 and 3.3 only) than the SPA's Seller Fundamental Representations, so the $3,000,000 Extended Holdback does not secure claims under the Tax (3.14) and Food Safety (3.17) representations. It locates this in Escrow Agreement Section 1.1 and/or 5.3, explains why this matters to the client, and recommends a fix.

The response identifies that the TSA lets Provider (Reitaisk) assign or delegate the TSA to any person without Trouseind's consent. It locates this in TSA Section 12.3, explains why this matters to the client, and recommends a fix.

The response identifies that the Escrow Agreement's Delaware governing law and exclusive Delaware Court of Chancery forum conflict with the SPA's New York law and New York County forum. It locates this in Escrow Agreement Section 10.2, explains why this matters to the client, and recommends a fix.

The response identifies that the side letter's nine-month survival for the Tax representation and the Pre-Closing Taxes indemnity expires (around December 31, 2026) before Seller's 2026 consolidated tax return covering the Company is even due. It locates this in Section 2 of the side letter, explains why this matters to the client, and recommends a fix.
The response states that the SPA's order of precedence gives the Escrow Agreement control over disbursement of Escrow Funds.
The response states that the SPA is governed by New York law.
The response is a memo whose issues are ordered with the items that matter most to the client first.
For each issue it lists, the response gives the document and section where it appears, why it matters for Trouseind, and a recommended fix.
The response claims that the side letter's nine-month survival period for the Tax representation is at least as protective for Trouseind as the SPA Section 9.1 tax survival period.
The response claims that the Escrow Agreement's definition of Fundamental Representation Claims includes the SPA Section 3.14 Tax representation.
